intro: Mukdahan is a Mekong riverside city where the food blends three traditions — Thai, Lao, and Vietnamese — producing flavours that are genuinely hard to find anywhere else. From a hot jaew hawn pot to a morning bowl of khao piak sen, all the way to nem nuong and grilled fish straight from the river, we've pulled together 10 restaurants that Mukdahan locals genuinely vouch for. Complete with locations, prices, and must-order dishes.
chips: 🐷 Crispy roast pork at Kaeng Krabao

blocks.html:
To tell a friend about Mukdahan, you have to start with the Mekong. This city sits directly opposite Savannakhet in Laos, connected by the Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge No. 2, and the food here reflects three cultures layered together in a way that's entirely its own. Walk through the Indochina market along the river and you'll see moo yor, nem nuong, khao piak sen, and Vietnamese snacks lined up together. The downtown area around Chayangkun Road and the old city holds the long-established local shops; Samran Chai Khong Road and Kaeng Krabao are the zones for eating by the river with a view. The charm of this city is that most restaurants are still family recipes passed down over decades.

This list includes legends like Wirin Jaew Hawn — the city's defining jaew hawn institution — Khao Piak Sen Jeh Sun & Chai Ton (Jao Gao), the original shop that has been selling for over thirty-six years with queues from early morning, and Sirichai Moo Han at Kaeng Krabao, a riverside crispy roast pork restaurant that even the provincial governor has recommended publicly. On the Vietnamese side there's Baan Lao Yuan Na Rim Khong and Krua Vietnam Mae Yo, both making nem nuong and fresh rolls with real depth of flavour. Nem nuong itself is a provincial signature recognised by the Mukdahan Chamber of Commerce. If you're passing through this city and don't try it, you've missed something. Scroll through the restaurants below and you'll see that Mukdahan takes eating more seriously than it looks.

blocks.name: Wirin Jaew Hawn
blocks.signature: Pork and plakang jaew hawn, pork bone broth, full basket of fresh vegetables, two-formula dipping sauce
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Mukdahan and want genuine local-style jaew hawn, Wirin Jaew Hawn is the restaurant that has to be on the list. The place has been open for many decades — a two-storey building with a warm antique feel, air-conditioned and comfortable, with around 6–8 tables tucked in a lane off Cha Phubal Road in the city. Good for a relaxed family meal or gathering a group around a hot pot.

The star of the restaurant is the pork and plakang (soldier fish) jaew hawn. The broth is simmered from pork bones until deeply fragrant — rich in colour but not overpowering in flavour, balanced in the way many reviewers call "gom glon" (well-rounded). Fresh plakang is firm-fleshed, the pork is tender, and a full large basket of fresh vegetables comes to cook in the pot as you like it. What people mention most often is the two-formula dipping sauce: one sweet and savoury jaew, one sharp seafood-style dipping sauce — mixing the two together makes it even better. Other well-regarded dishes include Vietnamese-style salad, salt-crusted chicken, and duck laab.

Prices run roughly 100–250 THB per head; the pork and plakang jaew hawn set is 300 THB. Good value given how many can eat from one pot and how much protein and vegetables come with it. Open daily approximately 10:00–22:00, easy to reach in the city.

One small note: parking in front of the restaurant is limited; some visitors park in the side lane. Some reviewers mention mosquitoes if you sit in the outer zone in the evening. Overall, people keep coming back for the bone-simmered broth and a flavour consistency that doesn't waver — making this the jaew hawn institution that Mukdahan locals are proud to bring visitors to.
blocks.bestFor: First meal in Mukdahan — groups and families
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: larb · Takeaway / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 3.0)

blocks.name: Khao Piak Sen Jeh Sun & Chai Ton (Original)
blocks.signature: Khao piak sen / Vietnamese-style kuayjab — pork bone broth fragrant with white pepper, chewy noodles topped with moo yor and fried spring onions
blocks.descHtml:
If you arrive in Mukdahan unsure where to start your first meal, Khao Piak Sen Jeh Sun & Chai Ton (the original shop) is the answer that locals give as a provincial institution. Running continuously for over 36 years, it has become a legendary restaurant in the Sri Boon Ruang area. The appeal is the khao piak sen and Vietnamese-style kuayjab using an original Vietnamese recipe — the broth is simmered from pork bones for a smooth, round flavour, lightly fragrant with white pepper, not overly salty. Good for both regular locals and visitors who want authentic Mukdahan taste.

The must-order is khao piak sen: fresh noodles that are smooth, chewy, and slide down cleanly, topped with minced pork, firm moo yor sausage, and fried spring onions that lift the whole bowl's aroma. Anyone who wants a fully loaded bowl can try the Vietnamese-style kuayjab with everything in one bowl. Reviews across the board read: clear but aromatic broth, bold flavour that's well-balanced, easy to eat and doesn't take long once the order goes in.

The atmosphere is a relaxed breakfast-style restaurant — easy to spot with its blue signage, seating for 11–40 people, with parking. Groups can order multiple bowls to share. Prices are very accessible — well under 100 THB per bowl. Location on Sri Boon Ruang Road next to River City Hotel, Mueang Mukdahan, convenient and close to the Mekong.

Worth knowing: the restaurant is open daily from 07:00 to midnight — workable as a morning meal before sightseeing or a late-night bowl after the night market. Weekend mornings get busy since it's a regular spot for locals. Coming before or after the rush avoids waiting. With consistency of flavour over decades and a flavour that never slips, this is the name Mukdahan people name first when someone asks for khao piak sen.
blocks.bestFor: First meal in the province — morning before sightseeing

blocks.name: Jeh Tuktah Khao Piak Sen (Next to the Fire Station)
blocks.signature: Loaded khao piak sen with savoury broth, chewy noodles, moo yor — also kuayjab and glass noodles with egg
blocks.descHtml:
Ask a Mukdahan local where to go for khao piak sen first thing in the morning and Khao Piak Dab Pleng (the nickname) — or its full name, Jeh Tuktah Khao Piak Sen Next to the Fire Station — is one of the first names out. The shop sits next to the municipal fire station on Wiwit Surakan Road in the old city. It's a small, open-air, home-style breakfast spot that has been part of the city for a long time. Perfect for anyone who's just arrived in Mukdahan and wants to start the day with something genuinely local — the way people in the city actually eat.

The star is the khao piak sen: chewy noodles with just the right bite, in a broth that multiple reviews describe as smooth and slightly sweet, loaded with moo yor, minced pork, and blood cake. Anyone who wants it heavier can add a poached egg. Beyond the khao piak sen there's Vietnamese-style thin-noodle kuayjab with egg, and glass noodles with egg for variety. Pair them with hot curry puffs and fried pa thong ko, and a warm cup of coffee or Ovaltine for a complete and satisfying morning meal.

Prices are genuinely very accessible: khao piak sen from 30 THB per bowl, blood topping adds 10 THB, poached egg 20 THB, curry puffs 5 THB each, pa thong ko 10 THB, drinks 20 THB. A full table meal and you're still not spending much. With local endorsement and an easy location in the city centre, this is the morning landmark people in Mukdahan bring visitors to try.

Worth knowing: the restaurant is open daily from 06:00 to around 13:00 — things can sell out before closing if you arrive late. Weekend mornings are busy and serving can slow down since it's a small team. Arriving before the peak or ordering takeaway works. Roadside parking next to the shop, easier to find earlier in the morning.
mustOrder: Loaded khao piak sen with moo yor

blocks.name: Chalongchai Pla Phao (Grilled Fish)
blocks.area: North Samran Chai Khong Road, Mueang Mukdahan District, Mukdahan
blocks.signature: Grilled fish, fresh Mekong tilapia dipped in jaew, tom yum plakang, pla look tao (crispy-fried tilapia)
blocks.descHtml:
If you come to Mukdahan and want to eat fresh Mekong fish the way locals eat it, Chalongchai Pla Phao is the name people in the area have been mentioning for a long time. This restaurant has been by the Mekong for over 40 years and is considered one of the original grilled-fish institutions of the city. The look of the restaurant is plain and unassuming, but once you've tasted the fish many people find themselves coming back. Good for a serious fish meal in a relaxed setting rather than a polished restaurant.

The must-order is pla phao — fresh fish selected by the restaurant and grilled over charcoal, served with jaew dipping sauce and fresh vegetables. Another dish people love is fresh Mekong tilapia dipped in jaew: the flesh is firm and clean, different from farmed tilapia. For broth, try tom yum plakang — a smooth, well-rounded broth that's assertive without being overwhelming — and pla look tao (tilapia cut into cubes and deep-fried until the outside is crispy and the inside stays moist). Spicier options like fish laab and gaeng om pla Mekong are also available for those who want to go bold.

The charm of the restaurant is the Mekong riverside location. Sitting comfortably looking across to the Laos bank, with plenty of seating, a relaxed atmosphere, and a cool breeze. The owner is welcoming and attentive to customers. Reviews consistently say: the restaurant looks ordinary but the food is not. Prices roughly 101–250 THB per head — fair for fresh river fish.

Open daily 08:00–22:00 at Ban Na Po Yai, North Samran Chai Khong Road, Mueang Mukdahan. Works for both lunch and dinner. For groups, ordering multiple fish preparations to share is the best approach. On weekend evenings it gets busy — calling ahead or pre-ordering a larger fish makes the visit smoother.
mustOrder: Fresh Mekong tilapia dipped in jaew
blocks.zone: Mekong riverside, North Samran Chai Khong
blocks.spice: Choose your level (laab / tom yum medium)
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: tom yum · Andy Li / Wikimedia (CC0)

blocks.name: Baan Lao Yuan Na Rim Khong
blocks.area: North Samran Chai Khong Road, Mueang Mukdahan District, Mukdahan
blocks.signature: Nem nuong, fried spring rolls, fried fish mieng, Lao-style som tum, home-style Thai-Lao-Vietnamese food
blocks.descHtml:
If you arrive in Mukdahan and want riverside food in a relaxed setting, Baan Lao Yuan Na Rim Khong is near the top of the list for most people. The restaurant sits at the start of North Samran Chai Khong Road right on the water, with a full view of the Mekong and the Laos bank. The selling point is three national cuisines in one restaurant — Thai, Lao, and home-style Vietnamese — ideal for families or groups of friends who want to order widely and share, sitting long with a view.

The dish nearly every table orders is nem nuong: minced pork marinated and grilled over charcoal, wrapped in soft rice paper with fresh vegetables and dipped in the restaurant's own house sauce. Next is crispy fried spring rolls, fried fish mieng (another standout dish), fiery Lao-style som tum, and fresh mieng rolls that genuine reviewers rate highly. Vietnamese food lovers can also try Vietnamese-style kuayjab and bun bo. Overall flavour reads as mid-range and approachable — not overwhelming — with generous portions per dish, good for sharing across multiple people.

Prices mostly 101–250 THB per head; some larger Vietnamese sets climb to 251–500 THB. Fair for the quantity and the riverside location. The restaurant has been updated to feel more modern, with both Mekong-view sitting and indoor zones, a cool breeze, and golden-hour light in the evenings that looks beautiful and photographs well. Parking in front and along the road, limited but enough. Open daily 10:00–22:00 (Saturdays–Sundays from 9:00).

For a riverside table in the evening, arriving early or calling ahead is wise — the restaurant is popular with both locals and visitors, and the best-view spots go quickly. A good USERS' CHOICE 2024 rating confirms it as a reliable riverside meal in Mukdahan.
blocks.bestFor: Riverside dinner watching the sunset — groups and families
blocks.spice: Medium (Lao som tum can be very spicy)

blocks.name: Krua Thai & Aitim Por Jai (Thai Kitchen & Ice Cream)
blocks.signature: Traditional fresh-coconut-milk ice cream, khao soi, single-dish Thai food
blocks.priceRange: 15–50 THB/ice cream, single-dish food under 100 THB
blocks.descHtml:
If you grew up near Mukdahan you probably know Krua Thai & Aitim Por Jai well — it's been part of the city for over thirty years, starting as a small ice-cream shop and gradually growing into a full Thai restaurant with both savoury dishes and desserts under one roof. Perfect for families looking for a relaxed spot, for visitors who want to taste something the city is known for, or for dessert lovers tracking down traditional fresh-coconut-milk ice cream that's getting harder to find every year.

The star is the fresh coconut milk ice cream made in-house — a clear, genuine coconut fragrance, available in multiple flavours: plain coconut, Thai tea, green tea, and chocolate. Genuine reviewers consistently say: "fragrant, fresh coconut milk" — and at prices starting in the single-digit tens, hard to believe how good it is. Eat it in a cup, a cone, or with bread. Choose your own toppings: sticky rice with coconut milk in a special house formula, roasted peanuts, sugar palm fruit, raisins, mung beans. For savoury food there's beef and chicken khao soi, dumplings, and single-dish Thai mains — a solid foundation before finishing with cold ice cream.

The atmosphere is casual and comfortable — unhurried, a natural family gathering spot for locals. Prices very accessible: ice cream roughly 15–50 THB, single-dish mains well under 100 THB per head. Wallet-friendly for a relaxed meal.

Location in the city on Phitak Santi Ratsadon Road near the Sri Boon Ruang area, easy to find. Open daily approximately 10:00–18:00. Worth noting: the restaurant often closes on Wednesdays — check before heading out. If you're passing through Mukdahan and haven't tried the fresh coconut milk ice cream here, it's a local favourite worth stopping for.
mustOrder: Traditional fresh coconut milk ice cream
Ice cream with sticky coconut rice
blocks.bestFor: Dessert lovers and families wanting to try the city's signature fresh coconut milk ice cream

blocks.name: Sirichai Moo Han Kaeng Krabao (Crispy Roast Pork)
blocks.area: Kaeng Krabao, Pa Ngkham Sub-district, Waan Yai District, Mukdahan
blocks.signature: Crispy-skin tender roast pork, Lao-style som tum, tom yum plakang, fish laab
blocks.descHtml:
If you come to Mukdahan without stopping at Kaeng Krabao, you haven't really arrived. And once you're at Kaeng Krabao, the first name locals will give you is Sirichai Moo Han — a large riverside restaurant that has been making crispy roast pork its centrepiece for so long it has become a legend of the area. Perfect for families or a big group of friends, since roast pig is sold whole and one pig split into two dishes feeds a good table for a serious meal.

The must-order is the moo han (roast pork): thin, genuinely crispy skin over tender young pork inside, served with two dipping sauces — sweet soy and a spicy version. Reviews suggest trying the sweet soy first. Beyond the roast pork, the Mekong fish menu is extensive: tom yum plakang with a bold, punchy flavour; fish laab; large-bowl Lao-style som tum; triple-crispy salad; and grilled fish — a full Isan riverside spread.

The atmosphere is a genuine bonus: a wide parking lot, stone tables, wooden tables, and bamboo pavilions in a long line right along the river, looking out over the wide Mekong bend stretching into the distance. The breeze is cool, the view is uninterrupted. Close to the Phaya Si Bhu Chang Muk Da Nakharat landmark — you can pay respects there then walk straight to lunch. Roast pork runs roughly 1,300–1,800 THB per whole pig depending on size; per head roughly 250–500 THB including side dishes. Fair for the quantity and the view.

The restaurant's popularity is genuinely earned — it has won the Users' Choice award and was recommended by the provincial governor publicly, generating press coverage. Thousands of check-ins on the Facebook page. Worth knowing: open daily approximately 08:00–18:00; on long weekends it fills up fast and daily roast pig quantities are limited. Call to reserve or arrive early if you want to be certain of getting one.
blocks.bestFor: Groups and families — riverside roast pork lunch
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: larb · Takeaway / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 3.0)

blocks.name: Krua Vietnam - Mae Yo
blocks.signature: Khanom buang yuan (Vietnamese crepes), fried spring rolls, nem nuong, mieng dip, original Vietnamese food
blocks.descHtml:
If you want genuinely traditional Vietnamese food in Mukdahan, Krua Vietnam - Mae Yo is a name that people in the city have been talking about for over 20 years. A small shop in the city centre near the Indochina market by the Mekong, using an original Vietnamese recipe passed down through generations — and recognised as a provincial speciality by the Mukdahan Chamber of Commerce. If you're exploring the riverside and want a great-value morning-to-midday meal, this is the spot for both locals and visitors.

The star is the nem nuong: minced pork marinated with spices and grilled until fragrant, firm-fleshed, wrapped in soft rice paper sheets with assorted fresh vegetables and dipped in the restaurant's own sauce — which many people describe as the real standout. A small set at around 150 THB feeds two people comfortably. Not to miss is the khanom buang yuan — crispy Vietnamese-style crepes with pork and bean sprout filling, paired with the nem nuong dipping sauce — and crispy fried spring rolls with a punchy dipping sauce and fresh chillies. Fans of hot food have the pan-fried egg, which many reviewers praise, as well as kanom jeen with toppings, Vietnamese kuayjab, and mieng dip (fresh wraps).

The atmosphere is a simple two-shophouse setup — not glamorous but clean and warm. The owner and staff are friendly and efficient. Prices per head mostly under 100 THB. That combination of value and quality is what brings people back repeatedly. Open from early morning to mid-afternoon, roughly 06:00.

One key thing to know: the restaurant is open only from morning through the afternoon and closes relatively early. If you want the full menu, arriving before 15:00 is safe. Weekend crowds can slow service since it's a small team, but the food is fresh and made to order — worth a short wait.
blocks.bestFor: Morning-to-midday before sightseeing — and Vietnamese food lovers
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: som tam · Vyacheslav Argenberg / Wikimedia (CC BY 4.0)

blocks.name: Jok Nong Ju (Porridge)
blocks.signature: Minced pork congee, pandan congee, pork blood tom, pork blood kao lao, stuffed bread
blocks.descHtml:
Ask a Mukdahan local what to eat first thing in the morning and Jok Nong Ju comes up near the top of the list every time. This is a legendary breakfast restaurant in the city — open long enough to have become the meeting point for office workers, elderly regulars, and visitors who want to start the day with a genuinely filling, hot meal. Perfect for anyone who wants a proper first meal of the day at a very easy price.

The dishes people order every visit: minced pork congee, cooked until the rice is silky fine, and pandan congee with a gentle, clean pandan fragrance that cuts through richness. For broth lovers, pork blood tom and pork blood kao lao are the stars — reviews consistently say the offal is clean and odour-free, the blood cake is soft, and the broth is rich and flavourful in a way that makes them the main event of the restaurant. Stuffed bread is a light snack alongside coffee. Anyone who wants something heavier can add a pan-fried egg, braised chicken rice, or kuayjab.

The atmosphere is a roadside stall under a canopy — simple but clean. The stand-out quality is fast service and a friendly, welcoming owner. Multiple reviewers warn that early mornings bring competition for tables like a game of musical chairs — coming after 09:00 makes for a calmer experience. Prices under 100 THB per head: pork blood kao lao around 60 THB, stuffed bread box 50 THB. Excellent value for a filling breakfast.

Location on Song Nang Sathit Road in the old city of Mukdahan, near the Sapphakon junction, close to the night market. Easy to reach. Open from around 05:00 to 14:00 daily. For visitors exploring the Mekong riverside who want breakfast the way locals eat it, this is the right answer. Things sell out quickly — arriving early means getting the full menu.
mustOrder: Pork blood tom / pork blood kao lao

blocks.name: Jice De' Cafe
blocks.signature: Drinks and desserts made from fresh garden coconut — signature bright-green menu items
blocks.descHtml:
If you're visiting Mukdahan and want a small, warm, characterful café to sit in, Jice De' Cafe is the one many people mention. The selling point is clear: nearly everything on the menu is made from fresh coconut sourced from the owners' own garden — drinks, desserts, most of the menu. The signature bright-green items photograph extremely well, the coconut frappe, coconut ice cream, and matcha coconut cream all get strong reviews, with a flavour that reads as refreshing, well-balanced sweetness, genuinely coconut. A natural match for Mukdahan's heat.

The café itself is small but thoughtfully decorated — clean white tones, rattan chairs, wooden tables, large arched windows for natural light, and a perforated wall that creates several beautiful photo spots. There's both an indoor zone and an outdoor section with white metal furniture against a brick wall. A detail many people love: colouring books and art supplies for sitting and drawing — fun for both children and adults. The overall feel is quiet and comfortable, good for sitting alone or bringing family or friends.

Prices are very accessible — roughly 50–130 THB per item, making it a café you can drop into without much thought. Location at Khumphon Lane, Chayangkun Road, Mukdahan city, next to the Mukdahan Teachers' Savings Cooperative — turn into the lane about 500 metres and it's on the left. Open daily during the daytime through evening. Parking both inside the property and in the lot across the bend from the shop.

One small note: the café is not large, and weekends can fill up. For the best photo angles or a table by the window, coming in the morning is better. Check the shop's page before visiting in case of any time adjustments on a given day. If you want a characterful small café with a clear identity and a coconut-forward menu you can't find elsewhere, this is worth the turn off the main road.
blocks.bestFor: Café-and-photo crowd — relaxed sitting with family or friends

blocks.title: Know before you eat in Mukdahan

items.title: Getting around the city
items.text: The city centre is small and many restaurants are walkable. Kaeng Krabao is outside the city and requires a vehicle. Grab has limited availability here — renting a car or motorbike is recommended, or negotiate a price with a songthaew or tuk-tuk driver before getting in.

items.title: Bring cash
items.text: Street stalls, breakfast shops, and the Mekong riverside market mostly operate on cash. Some shops have PromptPay or QR pay, but don't count on card payments. Carrying small notes and coins is most convenient.

items.title: Timing matters
items.text: Khao piak sen, congee, and breakfast shops often sell out before noon — go early if you want them. Riverside restaurants and roast pork at Kaeng Krabao get very busy on holiday evenings. Arriving before 18:00 or calling ahead avoids long waits.

items.title: Language and menus
items.text: Most local restaurants have Thai-only menus. English menus are rare. If communication is difficult, point at pictures on your phone or use a translation app. People in Mukdahan are friendly and always willing to recommend their best dishes if you tell them what you like.

items.title: Tipping
items.text: Street stalls and local restaurants don't expect tips — pay the stated price. At sit-down restaurants with table service, leaving a small amount of change is fine but not an obligation.

items.title: Say your spice level upfront
items.text: Isan and Lao food like Lao som tum, fish laab, and jaew are genuinely hot. If you can't handle heat, tell the seller you want less chilli or no chilli before they start preparing. You'll eat much better the whole meal.

blocks.title: Plan your eating in Mukdahan in one day
blocks.html:
If you have one day, this rhythm works well. Morning: khao piak sen at Jeh Sun & Chai Ton or Jeh Tuktah next to the fire station — these morning shops often sell out before noon. Follow up with Jok Nong Ju if you still have room, then a stop at Jice De' Cafe for a coconut drink to pace yourself.

Lunch through the afternoon: drive out to Kaeng Krabao and order a whole roast pig at Sirichai — split among the group with som tum alongside. Or if you're staying in the city, grilled fish at Chalongchai Pla Phao along the North Samran Chai Khong Road is equally satisfying. Round off the evening with jaew hawn at Wirin in the city, or sit at Baan Lao Yuan Na Rim Khong and order nem nuong with a Mekong breeze — all three flavours of Mukdahan in a single day.

blocks.text: When you're eating multiple meals in Mukdahan, staying overnight is far more relaxed than driving in and out. Wake up early and you'll be in time for the khao piak sen queue; save the riverside restaurants for the evening. Choose accommodation in the city near the Indochina market so the night market is a short walk away.

faq.q: Which Mukdahan restaurant is the most famous?
faq.a: By city-wide reputation, Wirin Jaew Hawn is the first jaew hawn institution people think of. For khao piak sen, Jeh Sun & Chai Ton (the original shop) is a 36-year legend. And Sirichai Moo Han at Kaeng Krabao is famous enough that the provincial governor publicly recommended it. All three are names Mukdahan people mention most often.

faq.q: What are the signature foods of Mukdahan?
faq.a: Mukdahan stands out for its three-culture Thai-Lao-Vietnamese food. The most distinctive signature is nem nuong, a provincial speciality recognised by the Mukdahan Chamber of Commerce. Next is khao piak sen and Vietnamese-style kuayjab eaten as breakfast. For riverside eating, Mekong grilled fish and Kaeng Krabao crispy roast pork are the addresses people give.

faq.q: How much does eating in Mukdahan cost?
faq.a: Morning shops like khao piak sen and congee are 30–80 THB per bowl. Cafés and ice cream run roughly 50–130 THB. Sit-down meals like jaew hawn, Vietnamese food, or grilled fish cost around 100–250 THB per head. Kaeng Krabao crispy roast pork is sold whole at 1,300–1,800 THB per pig — excellent value split among a group.

Street stalls and breakfast shops are walk-in — just go before things sell out. Riverside restaurants like Baan Lao Yuan or grilled fish places on weekend evenings get busy; calling ahead for a table is worthwhile. For Kaeng Krabao roast pork in a group, call ahead to pre-order the pig since quantities are limited daily.

faq.q: Which restaurants are open in the evening through to late night?
faq.a: For evenings, Wirin Jaew Hawn is a reliable hot-pot spot to sit comfortably. Riverside places like Chalongchai Pla Phao and Baan Lao Yuan Na Rim Khong are open through the evening. Some branches of Khao Piak Sen Jeh Sun & Chai Ton are also open late. In contrast, breakfast spots like Jok Nong Ju are morning-to-early afternoon only.
